localBiteReport: Reports from late October through mid-November point to a solid fall inshore bite on Choctawhatchee Bay. Redfish have been the most consistent target, with schools gathering around bridges, jetties, and East Pass — a charter angler reported landing two good-sized redfish under the bridge just this past week. Speckled trout in the 22–27-inch range have also been showing up wherever anglers can find bait concentrations, though fish remain somewhat scattered between late-summer and winter holding areas. Sheepshead are beginning to pick up at bridge pilings as water temps drop, and flounder are considered prime right now with November historically one of the best months of the year for them in the bay. Live shrimp, cut mullet on Carolina rigs, and soft plastics have all been producing; the most recent Destin-area reports note redfish feeding aggressively despite recent weather disruptions. Note: the most granular Choctawhatchee Bay-specific guide content in these reports is from the Oct 30–Nov 5 window, roughly 10 days ago — not same-week fresh.
